newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Selloff may double profits at CVRD - paper.
newsitem.headline: Selloff may double profits at CVRD - paper.

text.p: Profits at state-run Brazilian mining group Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) are likely to more than double after its privatization, which is to begin in early 1997, a local newspaper said.

Folha de S. Paulo, citing market analysts and officials at the National Development Bank (BNDES), said much of the hike in profits will be the result of the administrative flexibility the company will gain after it ceases to be a state firm.
The forecast also is partly based on the profits being posted by other large mining companies around the world, the paper said.

Last year, CVRD's net profit was equal to 3.2 percent of the firm's net worth compared with a worldwide average for mining firms of 15 percent and Brazilian miner Samitri's 9.2 percent, the paper said.
Vale posted a net profit of 111 million reais in 1997's first half.
